newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 cent per lb higher on Monday, although some traders said the market was likely to come in closer to unchanged and could even come under some pressure after monthly inventory data released late Friday showed an increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks.
Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in July by 219,000 60-kg bags, to 2,335,000 bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported.
Most industry sources expected the data to show a fairly modest build of 50,000-150,000 bags during July, although some dealers predicted a stock build of up to 250,000 bags.

Friday, New York arabicas ended sharply lower in anticipation of a build up in U.S. warehouse inventories. September fell 6.60 cents, to a three-week low of 177.95 cents, after ranging from 186.00 to 175.25 cents. December ended 4.20 cents lower, to 161.85 cents, while the back months closed down 3.10 cents.
September/December shrank to 16.10 cents compared with 18.50 cents at the close on Thursday. December/March 1998 narrowed to 15.75 cents versus 16.85 cents the previous session.
Technically, traders pegged September support at 175.00 cents, followed by 172.00 cents. Resistance was seen near 180.00 cents.
After Friday's close, the CSCE reported exchange-certified coffee stocks fell by 149 60-kg bags as of August 14, to 91,971 bags. An additional 7,500 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

Also after Friday's close, the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report for the two weeks ended August 12 showed non-commercial long positions decreased by 422 lots, to 2,872 lots. Non-commercial short positions decreased by 631 lots, to 658 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks fell by 647 lots, to 7,522 lots, while commercial short positions rose by 344 lots, to 12,965 lots.
Nonreportable long positions increased by 515 lots, to 10,121 lots and nonreportable short positions decreased by 267 lots, to 6,892 lots.

London robusta futures were down at midday on Monday, but off lows. LIFFE September fell $30 at the break, to $1,457, after ranging from $1,470 to $1,430. November was off $30, to $1,474, after sinking to $1,445.
